name: 2013 livery
description: White fuselage with 'IBERIA' in red over the forward windows; the fin is the Iberia symbol writ large: red with a white wedge and a yellow cap at the tip, and the red runs down off the fin over the aft fuselage and tail cone in a curve; white engines with the red title and symbol; red winglets.

areas.name: red over the aft fuselage, running down from the fin's root in a curve; the tail cone aft of it white

logos.description: The Iberia symbol: a small red shape like the fin, a white sliver and a yellow cap, set after the red 'IBERIA' on the cowling.

titles.style: Iberia's 2013 wordmark: red, bold, slightly rounded geometric capitals, upright, over the forward windows. Its baseline just above the window tops.
The wordmark small on the cowling, the symbol after it.

notes: Drawn from an A350 and an Iberia Express A321neo; the A320-family mainline aircraft weren't photographed for this pass (their engines may be red, as on Iberia Express). The fin's bands are drawn as straight wedges: on the aircraft they curve slightly. The red over the aft fuselage reaches the belly ahead of the stabiliser; its exact edge on the far side isn't seen. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on the A320neo EC-NDN (fitted to the A320 shape) and the A321neo EC-NIA: the title is much longer than drawn (x 0.18-0.324, about 5.4 m; it had been 0.1) and sits above the windows; the tail cone is white aft of x 0.90-0.94 (two photos agree; the red had run to the end); the red's forward edge drawn as a curve. Measured on the A320neo, the mainline's commonest short-haul type; Iberia Express A321neos carry 'EXPRESS' and aren't this scheme's titles.
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximation. The 2013 scheme replaced Landor's 1977 red-orange-yellow cheatline scheme, now retired.
